rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: UKHSA states that scarlet fever occurs most often in winter and spring.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: Symptoms can include a rash, sore throat, flushed cheeks and a swollen tongue.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: Scarlet fever is caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, also called group A streptococcus.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: Group A streptococci can occasionally cause severe and life-threatening disease.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: Scarlet fever is a notifiable disease in England and Wales.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: Health professionals must inform local health protection teams of suspected cases.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: Doctors can often diagnose scarlet fever from the clinical symptoms.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: A throat swab for bacterial culture can be used when laboratory confirmation is needed.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: Scarlet-fever risk depends on season, exposure, age, symptoms, setting, outbreak activity, diagnosis, treatment and reporting timing.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet-fever guidance and data
rows.verified: UKHSA scarlet-fever evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, season-, surveillance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: Gas appliances and fittings placed on the Great Britain market must meet applicable essential safety requirements.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: The gas-appliance regime assigns obligations to manufacturers, authorised representatives, importers and distributors.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: The regulations are intended to protect users, domestic animals and property from unsafe gas appliances.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: Approved Document J addresses air supply, discharge of combustion products and protection of buildings around combustion appliances.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: Common carbon-monoxide poisoning symptoms include headache, tiredness, difficulty thinking clearly and nausea.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: Cooking and heating appliances using fossil fuels should be regularly serviced by a qualified registered engineer.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: Adequate ventilation is required and chimneys and flues should be kept clear and maintained.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: An audible compliant carbon-monoxide alarm is an additional safeguard but is not a substitute for appliance servicing.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: Gas and carbon-monoxide risk depends on appliance design, fuel, installation, ventilation, flue condition, maintenance, use, occupancy and alarm coverage.

rows.source: OPSS and UKHSA gas-appliance and carbon-monoxide safety
rows.verified: OPSS and UKHSA gas-safety evidence is product-, installation-, building-, user-, maintenance-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level poisoning probability.
